title: Security & Compliance: RBAC, Audit Logging, Data Residency, Secure SDLC, Incident Response, Evidence Workflows, Risk & Exceptions
author: Alyssa Chen
content:
Summary

This page consolidates Redwood Inference’s operational policies and procedures for: RBAC and authentication, audit logging, data residency & retention, secure SDLC controls, security incident response, compliance evidence collection workflows, and risk/exception handling. The document is intended for engineering, security, and compliance stakeholders responsible for maintaining control evidence and for auditors performing assessments.

Scope

Applies to: all Redwood-hosted control planes, private deployments, Dedicated clusters, developer-facing APIs, admin consoles, CI/CD systems, and supporting infrastructure (IAM, logging, storage, KMS). Excludes: non-production research sandboxes unless explicitly enrolled in production-compliance program.

1) RBAC & Authentication

Objective: Ensure least-privilege access across services and clear ownership for all permissions changes.

Key controls:
- Centralized identity provider: Okta (OIDC) for employees + SAML for enterprise customers.
- Role model: predefined roles (admin, infra-engineer, platform-operator, product-analyst, support-agent) + resource-scoped roles for Dedicated and Private customer tenants.
- Just-in-time (JIT) elevation: short-lived admin sessions via privileged-access workflow (approval + MFA).
- Multi-factor auth: MFA required for all interactive accounts and for service account key creation.
- Service-to-service auth: mTLS with rotated certificates and short-lived tokens issued by internal token service.

Procedures:
1. Requesting access:
   1) Open an access request in the Access Portal with justification and duration.
   2) Owner approval required from resource owner and security.
   3) Access granted via IAM group membership with automatic expiry.
2. Role changes / audits:
   1) Quarterly RBAC review: owners receive a review task via Jira (task template: RBAC-REVIEW-YYYY-QX).
   2) Emergency role change: require 2 approvers and post-facto review within 48 hours.

RBAC Requirements Table:
| Item | Requirement | Owner | Frequency |
|------|-------------|-------|-----------|
| Role catalog | All roles documented, mappings to services | IAM Team | Continuous (update within 5 business days) |
| Access reviews | Owner attestations for all privileged groups | Resource Owners | Quarterly |
| JIT approvals | 2 approvers + MFA for admin sessions | Security | Real-time enforcement |

2) Audit Logging

Objective: Maintain tamper-evident records of critical events to support investigations, forensics, and compliance evidence.

What we log (minimum):
- Authentication events (success/failure, MFA challenges)
- Permission changes (role grants/revokes)
- Admin console actions (user creation, secrets management, deployment rollbacks)
- API key/service-account lifecycle events (create/rotate/revoke)
- Critical infra changes (network, firewall, routing, capacity allotment)
- Data access to customer-controlled data stores (read/write/delete)

Logging pipeline:
- Agents (Fluentd) -> Central logging cluster (Elasticsearch/Opensearch) -> Immutable archive (S3 bucket with Object Lock/Governance) -> SIEM (Splunk/Chronicle) for alerting and retention indexing.

Retention & Integrity:
- Operational logs: 1 year hot index (fast search), 3 years cold index (searchable), immutable archive 7 years (compliance).
- Audit logs (RBAC/auth, admin actions): 7 years immutable by default for enterprise customers, 3 years for standard accounts unless contract dictates otherwise.
- Hashing: daily manifest with SHA-256 checksums recorded in a signed ledger.

Logging Alerts & Playbooks:
- Alert: repeated failed logins (threshold: 10 within 10m) -> create incident, auto-disable account after 20 failed attempts pending review.
- Alert: unusual service token creation outside of CI -> auto-rotate environment token and notify owner.

3) Data Residency & Retention

Policy:
- Customers choose region(s) at onboarding; all customer data at rest is stored in the selected regions unless cross-region replication is explicitly enabled in the contract.
- Default retention policy for telemetry and aggregate metrics: 365 days.
- Customer-controlled content (prompt/response logs, embeddings, files): retention per customer contract and UI-configurable with guardrails (min 30d, max 10 years).

Data Residency Matrix:
| Data Type | Default Residency | Retention (default) | Encryption at rest | Owner |
|-----------|------------------|---------------------|--------------------|-------|
| Prompt/response logs | Customer region | 90 days (configurable) | KMS (customer-managed optional) | Product |
| Embeddings | Customer region | 90 days | KMS | Product |
| Audit logs | Primary region + immutable archive | 7 years | KMS | Security |
| Backups | Customer region + encrypted snapshots | 90 days | KMS | Infra |

Retention Procedures:
- Data deletion flow: 1) Customer requests deletion via Console or API -> 2) Deletion job queued -> 3) Job runs with verification (checksum + deletion report) -> 4) Evidence artifact created and stored in evidence repo.
- Legal hold: Security or Legal may escalate and place retention overrides (holds) with owner notification and documentation.

4) Secure SDLC

Goals: Integrate security gates throughout development to reduce vulnerabilities introduced to production.

Mandatory controls:
- Threat modeling: required for all services with public endpoints or that process customer data; to be completed during design PRD and updated pre-launch.
- Static Application Security Testing (SAST): run on PRs; failures for high severity block merge.
- Dependency scanning: SCA tools (e.g., Dependabot, Snyk) with automated patching or triage within 7 days for high severity.
- Dynamic security testing (DAST): monthly for all web-facing services and pre-major-release.
- Secrets scanning: on commit + CI gate; secrets found cause immediate pipeline failure.
- Container image signing and SBOM generation for all production images.

SDLC Workflow (numbered):
1. Design: security checklist + threat model attached to PRD.
2. Implement: branch-based development, WAF rules as infra-as-code when relevant.
3. Test: automated unit tests + SAST + SCA + DAST pre-merge.
4. Review: security reviewer tag required for sensitive services.
5. Release: gated by Canary + staged rollout + automated rollback policy.
6. Post-release: run automated smoke security tests and 24–72 hour monitoring window.

5) Incident Response — Security Procedures

Objective: Rapid detection, containment, and remediation of security incidents while preserving evidence and complying with notification obligations.

Incident lifecycle (high-level):
- Detection & Triage: alerts to PagerDuty (security-oncall) -> initial triage within 15 minutes.
- Containment: apply containment playbook (isolate host, revoke tokens, restrict network paths).
- Eradication: remove malicious artifacts, patch, rotate credentials.
- Recovery: restore services from known-good images/snapshots, verify integrity.
- Post-incident review: write postmortem, update controls, and publish to stakeholder channels.

Security incident SLAs:
- Acknowledge: 15 minutes for P1; 1 hour for P2.
- Initial containment actions: within 60 minutes for P1.
- Final remediation target: 72 hours for P1 (complex incidents may require extension with approvers).

Evidence and forensic preservation:
- Lockdown: create immutable snapshot of affected hosts (disk images) and logs; store copies in evidence S3 with Object Lock.
- Chain of custody: record who accessed the evidence artifact, reason, and timestamp.
- Forensic playbooks: include list of artifacts to collect (memory, running processes, /var/log, container runtime metadata, K8s audit logs).

6) Compliance Evidence Workflows

Purpose: Provide reproducible artifacts for auditors and internal reviews.

Evidence types and storage:
- Documentation: policy artifacts (this page, controlbook) stored in Confluence; signed attestation by owners.
- Config snapshots: IAM policies, RBAC manifests, security group configs stored in evidence repo (read-only).
- Logs & archives: hash-signed manifests + access logs pointing to immutable archives.
- Change evidence: Jira tickets, code reviews, terraform plan/apply outputs, signed release artifacts.

Evidence collection process (steps):
1) Evidence request received (internal audit or external auditor) via Compliance ticketing queue.
2) Evidence owner assigned (default mapping: security -> audit logs; infra -> backups; product -> data retention configs).
3) Owner populates evidence bundle in evidence repo with: narrative, artifacts, checksums, and access list.
4) Compliance performs verification and signs off.

Evidence Delivery options:
- Temporary auditor access: timeboxed, scoped IAM role + monitoring + NDA verification.
- Copy export: curated bundle with checksums delivered to auditor SFTP with access expiry.

7) Risk & Exceptions

When a control cannot be met, teams must follow an exceptions process rather than bypassing controls.

Exception process:
1. Submit exception request with justification, compensating controls, and duration.
2. Initial review by Control Owner.
3. Risk assessment by Security (qualitative + quantitative: likelyhood x impact).
4. Approval levels:
   - Low risk: Security approver.
   - Medium risk: Security + Infra engineering manager.
   - High risk: Security, CTO, and Legal.
5. Exceptions granted with expiration and mandatory mitigation plan.

Exception record fields (must be provided):
- Title, owner, affected services, justification, compensating controls, risk rating, expiration date, reviewers, approval chain.

8) Ownership & Contacts

Primary owners:
- IAM & Access Controls: Ravi Patel (IAM Team) — iam-team@redwood.ai
- Audit Logging & SIEM: Marta Lopez (Security Ops) — secops@redwood.ai

- Secure SDLC: Ethan Brooks (Engineering Security) — engsec@redwood.ai

Escalation matrix (summary):
- 0–15m: PagerDuty alert -> security-oncall
- 15–60m: Security Manager -> cross-team incident bridge
- 60m+: CTO & Legal notified for P1 and potential customer impact

Appendix A — CLI & API Examples

Sample: request deletion for customer content via API

curl -X POST "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/admin/data/deletion" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"customer_id":"cust_12345","data_types":["prompts","embeddings"],"requested_by":"owner@example.com"}'

Sample: evidence bundle structure (manifest example)

manifest.json
{
  "bundle_id": "evidence-2027-11-10-0001",
  "owner": "compliance@redwood.ai",
  "items": ["iam-policy-2027-10-01.json","audit-log-manifest-2027-11-10.csv"],
  "checksum": "sha256:..."
}

Appendix B — Quick Reference Table: Retention & Owners
| Artifact | Retention | Owner | Archive Location |
|---------|-----------|-------|------------------|
| Auth events | 3 years (hot 1yr) | Security | s3://evidence/auth-events/ |
| Admin actions | 7 years | Security | s3://evidence/admin-actions/ |
| Customer content | contract-defined | Product | customer-region-snapshots |
